findings.description: RootModel sets `__pydantic_private__ = None` as a class attribute, which shadows the BaseModel slot, so a subclass's private attributes live in the instance `__dict__`. The removed block copied that private dict and dropped `PydanticUndefined` placeholders. `new_dict = copy(self.__dict__)` is only shallow, so after this change the copy and the original share the same private dict. Setting a private attribute on one therefore changes the other. Unset private attributes also stay as `PydanticUndefined` in the copy, so reading them returns the sentinel instead of raising AttributeError.
findings.suggestion: Restore the handling: after copying `__dict__`, replace `__pydantic_private__` with a new dict that omits `PydanticUndefined` values.
